subject: technology
topic: Shopping sites are built to push you with tricks you rarely notice
angle: Dark patterns are profit-maximizing design choices that successfully manipulate consumers into making unintended purchases, with limited-time messages being particularly effective.
title: The Architecture of Choice

reveal.headline: Shopping sites use design to maximize profit.
reveal.body: Firms use proprietary A-B testing to confirm that dark patterns are profit maximizing. These design choices successfully manipulate consumers into making unintended purchases.

explain.headline: Design choice drives your spending.
explain.body: Decision architecture, rather than the price of an item, drives your purchasing decisions. Researchers found that people are significantly more likely to select products with dark patterns.

matters.headline: Your choices are not yours alone.
matters.body: That may be why you feel pushed toward a purchase. The systems you use are designed to influence your behavior through specific messages and layouts.

example.headline: A countdown clock on a screen.
example.body: You see a timer ticking down on a product page. The message says the offer expires in minutes. You click the button to buy it now.

verdict: The evidence confirms that dark patterns are widespread and effective at influencing consumer behavior to maximize profit.
caveat: The study on awareness interventions found no clear evidence that video- or activity-based methods effectively reduce the impact of dark patterns.
caption:
Shopping sites use specific design choices to influence your behavior. 

Research shows that dark patterns are widespread and effective at maximizing profit. While some methods were tested to reduce their impact, there is currently no clear evidence that video- or activity-based methods work.
